cases.title: Shelter at the Mountain Shrine
cases.subtitle: 山祠避雨 · Thunder, dripping water & distant bells
cases.text: 山祠外雷声滚过，采药人叶青扶着受伤的樵夫避进殿里，草鞋在泥地上啪嗒作响。漏雨从瓦缝滴进陶钵，嗒嗒不停；她掀开旧帘，布面哗啦抖出积尘。祠后忽然传来鹿的短鸣，叶青循着声音找到干草和净水，木桶碰井沿咚的一声。她替樵夫包好脚踝，等山路上的驮队铜铃靠近，才将人交给熟识的赶路人。
cases.note: Drip sequence replaced pouring/fire-like candidates; bucket impact and approaching bells audible in local mixed review. Animal cue is audible but exact deer species identity is not independently established; not a claim of a field recording.

cases.title: The Storm-Damaged Shrine
cases.subtitle: A quiet rain bed & a sudden collapse
cases.text: Sheltering from rain in a mountain shrine, an old carpenter heard a faint crack from a roof beam and suspected that its joint had loosened. His footsteps thudded over damp bricks as he held up a flame to inspect the split. Rain pattered densely on the tiles, and a gust scattered ash from the incense burner across the floor. He hurriedly struck a small bronze bell to warn everyone out of the side hall. A moment later the rotten beam fell with a crash, but no one was hurt. He cordoned off the area and promised the shrine keeper that he would return to repair the roof when the weather cleared.
cases.note: Faint crack identified in mixed clip with clean control; do not demand a heavy crash for a faint warning. Rain seam repaired, brief gust strengthened, bell and later collapse retained. Separate audible dust grains are not mandatory.

cases.title: The Painter’s Scroll
cases.subtitle: 画师与卷轴 · Window impact, rain & unfurling cloth
cases.text: 山祠里寄住的画师怕雨毁了新画，抱卷轴跑过石阶，鞋跟嗒嗒响。风撞开木窗，窗扇砰地拍墙，雨水沙沙扫过纸屏。他请守祠老人帮忙压住画角，老人用铜镇纸叮地落案。两人卷起画布时，绢面呼啦收拢，露出画背写着的失散名单。老人认出其中一位是自己的女儿，决定天一亮便下山打听，不再独自守着空殿。
cases.note: Steps, window impact, rain and cloth have supporting source/mixed evidence. Metal contact exists at corrected 14.412-second anchor, but local mixed listening cannot reliably identify it despite source changes and format control. Final perceptual acceptance is withheld.

cases.title: A Warning in the Print Shop
cases.subtitle: Mechanical rhythm & a spoken intervention
cases.text: A troupe wanted new songbooks printed, but the printshop owner saw that the leading character's name kept coming out crooked. She tapped the copper plate lightly on the desk; a bright ding revealed a thin thread in its seam. Night rain rustled across the roof tiles outside. Someone fled through puddles by the back door, wet footsteps fading away, and the wooden latch rattled against the frame. At the mouth of the alley she heard the candyman striking his small copper gong and asked him to stop the fugitive. She tore open the recovered paper packet with a rustle. Inside were the old lyrics: someone had feared the new play would expose a long-ago impersonation.
cases.note: Copper contact identified in mixed clip with clean control after correcting gain-edit ID. Rain, wet steps, latch, gong and paper remain. Full-listener missing-ding judgement conflicts with local evidence and is retained, not erased.

cases.title: The Floodgate
cases.subtitle: 守闸 · Stone, chains & rushing water
cases.text: 暴雨将至，守闸的顾七发现上游水位突然涨过红线。他踩着石阶跑进闸房，鞋底啪嗒作响；檐角的雨珠滴进铜盆，叮叮连响。顾七拽动铁链，链环哗啦碰撞，沉重闸板却只挪了一寸。他叫徒弟敲响岸边铜锣，村人推着木车沿堤赶来，车轮吱呀滚过碎石。众人合力清出卡住闸槽的断木，水终于轰地冲向备用河道，低处的屋舍保住了。
cases.note: New hard-surface steps and chain friction identified in mixed/control comparison; gate friction and repaired wood movement are physically compatible. Gong now independently audible. Opening storm is a design bed, not a requirement for literal rainfall before the storm.

cases.title: The Sluice Keeper
cases.subtitle: Metal impacts against moving water
cases.text: A county painter came to redraw the old sluice gate, but found that someone had quietly replaced its measuring ruler. At dawn he climbed mossy steps, his wooden clogs tapping the stone, while water ran steadily through the sluice tunnel. He tapped the ruler with a small hammer: the old wood sounded dull, but the new wood answered with a hollow knock. He pulled a hidden nail, and an iron plate clanged into a basin. Outside, the gatekeeper rang the departure bell. The painter held up the faulty ruler; the boatmen stopped rowing, leaving only small waves lapping the bank. The gate was sealed before it could be opened by mistake.
cases.note: Clog steps are identified in mixed clip with clean speech control; distinct wooden contacts and metal/bell cues remain. Water tail silence repaired; flowing water transitions to separate small waves. Extra rowing foley is not mandated by the text.

cases.title: The Printing House
cases.subtitle: 印坊 · A press, scattered paper & a warning
cases.text: 印坊赶制赈灾告示，学徒小泉却听见压版机每转一圈都发出异样的嘎哒声。他沿长桌走过去，木地板咚咚回响，掀起纸堆时纸页哗啦散开。砚台被人推落，啪地碎成两半，他在碎片下找到调换的铜字。院里驴车铃声已响，押运人催着发车。小泉喊停师傅，用木槌逐字敲回正确版面，滚筒重新吱呀转起时，百姓看见的才是真正的放粮日期。
cases.note: Rhythmic press, steps, rustling paper, bells and roller friction are supported by source and mixed observations. A narration-only bell false positive is retained and weakens that individual model statement; source-only jingling provides separate support.

cases.title: The Blacksmith’s Hairpin
cases.subtitle: Wet steps, bellows & the forge
cases.text: A blacksmith's apprentice accidentally snapped a bride's hairpin, with barely enough time left before the wedding procession. Clutching its box, he ran down the stone street, his shoes splashing through muddy water. Inside the forge, the bellows pumped steadily and the fire crackled higher. His master told him to slow down. He straightened the ornament with small, ringing hammer taps, wound the silver wire back into place, and closed the pliers with a sharp click. Wedding drums drew nearer from the street. He polished the hairpin and returned it before the bridal sedan stopped at the door.
cases.note: Wet steps now observed as splashing steps; bellows pumping and fire identified together with clean speech control. Hammer/click/drums remain. Extra polishing and wire-twisting cues are optional rather than mandatory omissions.

cases.title: A Night at the Inn
cases.subtitle: 寒夜客栈 · Fire, a falling lid & hurried steps
cases.text: 寒夜客栈住进一队迷路镖师，灶娘桂婶听出后院有人偷翻米缸。她踩过灶前碎柴，咔嚓一声；柴火在锅底噼啪作响，木勺搅汤哗啦转圈。桂婶没有惊动客人，只把铜锅盖轻扣在后门，门一开便当啷坠地。小贼沿湿巷逃跑，脚步啪嗒急促，原来只是饿得发抖的邻村孩子。桂婶给他盛了粥，再请镖师送他回去。
cases.note: Dry snap, fire, stirring, two separate lid actions and wet running remain in the plan. Replaced wet steps and lid impact are supported by isolated and mixed evidence. Narration-control false positives prevent treating all listener labels as ground truth.

cases.title: Sacks at the Watermill
cases.subtitle: Leaves, wooden impacts & the mill
cases.text: The granary claimed that the watermill had swallowed three sacks of wheat, and its owner could not defend himself. At night he heard the low hum of the millstone spinning empty. He ran along the stone path, dry leaves rustling underfoot. Wind slapped the back window against its frame, while the wooden grain hopper rocked with a soft clunk. He lifted a floorboard; an iron ring rattled against a hidden door, revealing the missing sacks. He beat a wooden clapper to summon the bookkeeper, its knocks carrying toward the village entrance. The bookkeeper recognized the hidden flood passage: the wheat had been swept into it by the water.
cases.note: Window impacts identified in mixed clip with clean control; hopper has a soft contact and wood friction precedes the iron-ring action. Window reduced to avoid dominating narration. Exact object identity of friction/impact foley remains approximate.
